{{ElectionsIA}}
The '''2026 Iowa gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Iowa]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] businessman Zach Lahn and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state auditor [[Rob Sand]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican incumbent [[Kim Reynolds]] is not seeking a third term.

[[Primary elections]] were held on June 2, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=January 1, 2025|title=State of Iowa Election Calendar 2026|url=https://sos.iowa.gov/elections/pdf/cal3yr.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260521023253/https://sos.iowa.gov/elections/pdf/cal3yr.pdf|archive-date=May 21, 2026|access-date=April 18, 2025|publisher=[[Secretary of State of Iowa]]}}</ref> In the Republican primary, congressman [[Randy Feenstra]] emerged as the frontrunner after being endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], but Lahn won the nomination in an [[Upset (competition)|upset]] with 37.65% of the vote. Sand was the only candidate to qualify for the ballot in the Democratic primary.

This is the first open gubernatorial election in Iowa since [[2006 Iowa gubernatorial election|2006]] and the first to be held at the same time as the [[2026 United States Senate election in Iowa|open Senate election]] since [[1968 Iowa gubernatorial election|1968]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Could Iowa Democrats Win 2026's Gubernatorial and US Senate Races? |url=https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2026/06/03/could-iowa-democrats-win-2026s-gubernatorial-and-us-senate-races/ |work=Smart Politics |date=June 3, 2026 |accessdate=June 6, 2026}}</ref> The 2006 gubernatorial election is the most recent won by Democrats in Iowa.

== Background ==
[[Iowa]] is considered to be a moderate-to-strong [[Red states and blue states|red state]], with both chambers of its state legislature controlled by the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. However, in [[2025 Iowa elections#State legislative|special elections in 2025]], Iowa Republicans lost their supermajority in the [[Iowa Senate]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Democrat Renee Hardman wins Iowa state Senate seat, blocking GOP from reclaiming supermajority |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/amp/politics/democrat-renee-hardman-wins-iowa-state-senate-seat-blocking-gop-from-reclaiming-supermajority |access-date=October 7, 2026 |publisher=PBS |date=December 31, 2025}}</ref> Republicans still maintain their supermajority in the [[Iowa House of Representatives]] that they won in [[2024 Iowa House of Representatives election|2024]].<ref>{{cite news |title=GOP at risk of significant state legislative losses, Post analysis finds |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/06/its-not-just-congress-how-midterms-can-reshape-state-by-state-power/ |access-date=October 7, 2026 |publisher=Washington Post |date=October 6, 2026}}</ref> The last time the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] won a gubernatorial election in Iowa was in [[2006 Iowa gubernatorial election|2006]]. All 4 members of the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] from Iowa have been Republicans since [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa|2022]] and Republicans have won all [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] elections in Iowa since 2010, making Iowa's congressional delegation entirely Republican. Iowa has voted for Republican presidents since [[2016 United States presidential election in Iowa|2016]], trending in favor of the Republican Party increasingly since then.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCue |first=Dan |title=Des Moines Register Poll Reconfirms Iowa’s Shift From Swing to Red State |url=https://www.thewellnews.com/opinion-polls/des-moines-register-poll-reconfirms-iowas-shift-from-swing-to-red-state/ |access-date=July 27, 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref> Sand was the only Democratic candidate who statewide in [[2022 Iowa elections|2022]], as he won the [[2022_Iowa_State_Auditor_election|state auditor election]] by just 2,893 votes.<ref>{{cite news |title=Democrat Rob Sand wins state auditor’s race, Todd Halbur concedes |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2022/11/19/democrat-rob-sand-wins-state-auditors-race-todd-halbur-concedes/ |access-date=October 7, 2026 |publisher=Daily Iowan |date=November 19, 2022}}</ref>

== Libertarian primary ==
=== Candidates ===
On June 2, the Gluba campaign submitted over 8,000 signatures to the Iowa Secretary of State, satisfying the 3,500 signature requirement to qualify for the ballot.<ref name=":1" /> However, later he got disqualified from the ballot as he did not follow the proper legal procedures when trying to substitute his running mate.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url = https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/08/27/libertarian-party-lawsuit-iowa-governor-congress-candidates-nominees/91481453007/| title = Iowa Libertarians lose lawsuit to replace governor, Congress candidates on November ballot| last = Meiss| first = Veronica|date = August 28, 2026 |website = The Des Moines Register| access-date = September 4, 2026}}</ref>

====Disqualified====
*Nicholas Gluba, [[Lone Tree, Iowa|Lone Tree]] city councilor and nominee for {{ushr|IA|1}} in [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 1|2024]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=IOWA |first=LIBERTARIAN PARTY OF |date=June 5, 2026 |title=Nicholas Gluba Secures Ballot Access for Iowa Governor Race |url=https://www.communitynewspapergroup.com/nicholas-gluba-secures-ballot-access-for-iowa-governor-race/article_9b02157c-3143-44e3-bc15-08d9a6af70a0.html |access-date=June 9, 2026 |website=Community Newspaper Group |language=en}}</ref><ref name="auto"/>

===Candidates===
====Did not qualify====
*Sondra Wilson, pre-law student<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pfannenstiel |first1=Brianne |title=2026 Iowa governor's race: Who's in, who's out and who's on the fence |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2025/07/28/iowa-governor-race-2026-heres-whos-running-democrats-republicans/85341426007/ |access-date=November 5, 2025 |work=Des Moines Register |date=July 28, 2025 |quote=Ames resident and Iowa State University student Sondra Wilson has filed paperwork with the Iowa Ethics and Campaign Disclosure Board to run for governor as a no-party candidate in 2026.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Sondra |title=Independent Gubernatorial Candidate Sondra Wilson Asks Iowa Supreme Court to Restore Her Path to the Ballot. |url=https://wildwillpower.org/wilson-v-pate-the-ballot-extension-case |website=Wild Willpower PAC |date=August 22, 2026}}</ref> ''(previously ran as a Democrat)''<ref>{{cite web |last1=James |first1=Kayla |title=Democrat Sondra Wilson advocates for housing, health and LGBTQ+ rights in Iowa governor bid |url=https://www.kcci.com/article/democrat-sondra-wilson-iowa-governor-race/64984503 |access-date=November 4, 2025 |publisher=[[KCCI]] |date=June 5, 2025}}</ref>

== General election ==

=== Campaign ===
Though originally from Iowa, Zach Lahn faced scrutiny following reporting by ''[[The Des Moines Register]]'' that he lived in [[Kansas]] until 2023, when he allegedly returned to Iowa.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Henderson |first=O. Kay |date=June 5, 2026 |title=Sand suggests Lahn should have run for governor in another state - Radio Iowa |url=https://www.radioiowa.com/2026/06/05/sand-suggests-lahn-should-have-run-for-governor-in-another-state/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260607080158/https://www.radioiowa.com/2026/06/05/sand-suggests-lahn-should-have-run-for-governor-in-another-state/ |archive-date=June 7, 2026 |access-date=July 2, 2026 |work=Radio Iowa |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> Lahn registered to vote in [[Iowa]] on October 17, 2024, ahead of the 2024 election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carpenter |first=Tim |date=May 29, 2026 |title=Co-founder of Wichita private school contending for Iowa GOP's gubernatorial nomination • Kansas Reflector |url=https://kansasreflector.com/2026/05/29/co-founder-of-wichita-private-school-contending-for-iowa-gops-gubernatorial-nomination/ |access-date=July 7, 2026 |website=Kansas Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref> The newspaper later reported that flight records indicated Lahn spent 75 nights in [[Wichita, Kansas]] between October 2025 and spring 2026, frequently traveling there by private plane.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Larson |first=Luke |date=June 19, 2026 |title=Lahn defends Iowa residency amid campaign criticism |url=https://who13.com/news/politics/iowa-politics/lahn-defends-iowa-residency-amid-campaign-criticism/ |website=WHO13 Des Moines}}</ref> Lahn said the trips were related to custody arrangements involving his children, who live in Kansas. 

Rob Sand criticized Lahn as a "part-time Iowan" and a [[Carpetbagger (politics)|carpetbagger]], arguing that his frequent travel to Kansas conflicted with his "Iowa First" campaign message. Sand, meanwhile, has faced criticism from Governor Kim Reynolds and other state Republicans, who have accused him of using high-profile audits and allegations of fraud to bolster his political profile.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Luu |first=Isabella |date=January 6, 2026 |title=State Auditor Rob Sand lays out legislative priorities for 2026 session |url=https://www.iowapublicradio.org/state-government-news/2026-01-06/state-auditor-rob-sand-priorities-2026-legislative-session |access-date=August 12, 2026 |website=Iowa Public Radio |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Henderson |first=O. Kay |date=February 18, 2025 |title=Auditor, governor quarrel over access to E.S.A. information - Radio Iowa |url=https://www.radioiowa.com/2025/02/18/auditor-governor-quarrell-over-access-to-e-s-a-information/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724203522/https://www.radioiowa.com/2025/02/18/auditor-governor-quarrell-over-access-to-e-s-a-information/ |archive-date=July 24, 2025 |access-date=August 12, 2026 |work=Radio Iowa |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> 

In early September, ''[[The Des Moines Register]]'' reported that the [[Black Hawk County, Iowa|Black Hawk County]] Sheriff's Office was investigating Lahn's running mate, Wulf, for theft and fraud in relation to accusations that Wulf had misled lenders and business associates about his finances.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lenders, farmers accuse Lt. Gov candidate Derek Wulf of theft, fraud|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/09/04/republican-derek-wulf-finances-fraud-iowa-election-zach-lahn/91251482007/|first=Tyler|last=Jett|date=September 4, 2026|access-date=September 4, 2026|website=[[The Des Moines Register]]}}</ref>
